$comment: EnergyX Trust Layer — fact registry v2.
PROVENANCE, read this before demoing anything:
- The 'lh-*' facts were measured by Raj from Lighthouse 13.5.0 reports he ran
on 2026-10-08. He has the report URLs. These are solid.
- The 'ex-*' facts were read off energyx.com on 2026-10-08 via an automated
page fetch. They are marked verified:true so the assistant can use them,
BUT a transcription error is possible.
- Checked by hand against the live site on 2026-11-08, each matching the page it
cites: ex-ceo, ex-cmo, ex-patents, ex-funding, ex-dle-time, ex-water-reduction,
ex-bg-capacity, ex-gm. Their 'accessed' dates are that day. Facts not on this
list keep their 2026-10-08 date and have not been re-checked since.
- The 'lh2-*' facts are Raj's re-measurement of 2026-11-10 (lighthouse-metrics.com, Lighthouse 13.5.0,
mobile preset, US West, one run per page). The October lh-* and demo-* figures are kept, with
their own dates. Bytes were NOT re-measured on 2026-11-10: every weight figure is from October.
The check pages are account-scoped, so each lh2-* source is the saved report PDF in
public/evidence/lighthouse-2026-11-10/, served from this demo behind its basic auth.
approvedAt is null on every EnergyX fact, always. Raj is not EnergyX.
basisSource: 'stated' means the cited source itself says what the figure
counts. 'inferred' means it does not, and the basis here is this registry's
reading. The gap between those two is the entire point of the project.
Byte facts (unit 'KiB'): numeric is KiB exactly as Lighthouse reports it;
value is decimal MB = KiB * 1024 / 1e6, one decimal place.
tests/unit/byte-facts.test.ts recomputes every one.

facts.label: DLE processing time
facts.basis: Figure given in the homepage comparison table, contrasted against 12 to 18 months for conventional evaporation. The table does not define what counts as the start or end of the process.

source.title: EnergyX homepage, conventional vs DLE comparison

alsoPublishedAs.basis: Stated in the FAQ section of the same homepage: direct lithium extraction reduces the conventional timeline to hours.

Stated on the FAQ page, in the answer to "What is the typical processing time for GET-Lit™?": "Using our GET-Lit™ DLE technology as a standalone solution, lithium extraction can be completed within hours to days, depending on site-specific factors." The answer does not say where the clock starts or stops.

Shown in the Quick Facts on the lithium page, labelled "Continuous Process". The technology page (https://energyx.com/technology/) serves the same content. The label does not say where the clock starts or stops, so what this figure measures is this registry's reading.

facts.note: Both figures appear on the SAME page. This is the clearest example in the registry: one subject, two published answers, neither stating what it measures. Present it as a metadata gap, never as an error.

facts.label: Freshwater reduction vs conventional extraction
facts.basis: Described in the homepage FAQ as the reduction achieved versus conventional extraction. The FAQ also gives the underlying figures: up to 400,000 gallons per ton conventional, around 800 gallons per ton with DLE.
facts.note: The two figures EnergyX publishes imply roughly a 99.8% reduction, not 'over 90%'. Technically 99.8% IS over 90%, so the claim is not wrong — it is conservative to the point of hiding its own strength. This is the one finding in the registry where the correction makes EnergyX's claim stronger. Lead with it when talking to the CMO.

facts.label: Freshwater use, conventional extraction
facts.basis: Stated in the homepage FAQ as the freshwater consumption of conventional extraction per ton of lithium.

alsoPublishedAs.basis: Stated on the sustainability page: "Current brine evaporation uses 500K gallons water/ton lithium in communities already dealing with water scarcity." The sentence gives no basis for the figure, such as the site, the year or the method it was counted by.

facts.label: Freshwater use, EnergyX DLE
facts.basis: Stated in the homepage FAQ as EnergyX's freshwater consumption per ton of lithium.

facts.label: Freshwater reduction implied by EnergyX's own figures
facts.basis: Arithmetic by this registry from two figures in the homepage FAQ: around 800 gallons per ton with DLE against up to 400,000 gallons per ton conventional. EnergyX does not publish this percentage; the same FAQ states the reduction as over 90%.
facts.note: tests/unit/byte-facts.test.ts recomputes this from ex-water-conventional and ex-water-dle.

facts.label: Patents
facts.basis: Figure in the homepage company-stats band. The homepage does not state whether this counts granted patents only, or granted plus pending applications, or which technology areas are included.

alsoPublishedAs.basis: The blog post says "Backed by more than 150 patents" in its body and "backed by 150+ patents" in its Key Takeaways. It says patents; it does not say whether that counts granted patents, applications or both. An earlier basis for this figure assumed applications were included. That assumption was wrong: the post does not say so.

facts.note: Checked 2026-11-08: neither the homepage band (140+) nor the blog post (150+) says what its count includes, whether granted patents, applications or both. So the homepage is not the only page without a basis for this figure; the blog has none either. The SEC filings an earlier version of this note mentioned have not been checked.

facts.label: Black Giant capacity
facts.basis: Given on the homepage project card as Phase I and II combined. This is a planned capacity, not current production.
facts.note: What the Black Giant project page (https://energyx.com/black-giant/) says, checked 2026-11-08: under Production Target it lists 7,500 tpa LCE (Phase I) in 2028 and 52,500 tpa LCE (Phase II) in 2030, then 100,000 tpa LCE (Phase III) and 150,000 tpa LCE (Phase IV), both dated TBD. Its header gives a project size of 52,500 tpa LCE, and its Browse projects card repeats 53Ktpa LCE Phase I & II. What it does not say: whether the 52,500 is cumulative or Phase II alone, or how 52,500 relates to 53K. Phase I and Phase II as listed sum to 60,000, which matches neither figure. So this registry does not treat 52,500 and 53K as one figure shown two ways.

facts.label: Black Giant in-situ resource
facts.basis: Given on the homepage project card as an in-situ figure. An in-situ resource is lithium estimated to be present in the ground, not lithium that is recoverable or economic to produce.

facts.label: Lonestar DOE grant

facts.label: Lonestar target capacity

facts.label: Powder Hound capacity
facts.basis: Given on the homepage project card as projected capacity for a commercial DLE facility at the Great Salt Lake, Ogden, Utah, with Compass Minerals.
facts.note: Use the precise noun for the Compass Minerals relationship. The homepage says 'with Compass Minerals'; earlier reporting described a non-binding MOU. Do not upgrade it to a partnership without a source that says so.

facts.label: Share of first-load JavaScript that is React DOM and the Next app-router client (local)
facts.basis: The two largest shared scripts, identified by the library code they contain (React DOM's Fiber and hydrateRoot code; the app router's prefetch and navigation code), total 119,777 compressed bytes of the 145,660 that every route except the Black Giant page loads. Measured on 2026-11-03 against a local `next start`, 390px viewport, by listing each script request with Playwright. Attribution is by library fingerprint, not module-level attribution, so the boundary of each library is not module-exact. Rounded to a whole percent.

facts.label: Share of first-load JavaScript in the one script that is this site's own code (local)
facts.basis: The AskForm script, the only script that is this repo's own code rather than shared with a framework component, is 2,659 compressed bytes of the 145,660 that every route except the Black Giant page loads. Measured on 2026-11-03 against a local `next start`, 390px viewport. The mobile menu shares a script with next/link and the hero video with next/image; those were not separated, so this is a floor for this site's code, not a total. Attribution is by library fingerprint, not module-level attribution, so it is not module-exact. Rounded to a whole percent.

facts.label: Size of the one script only the Black Giant page loads (local)
facts.basis: The Black Giant page requests one script no other route does: 7,168 compressed bytes on the wire (headers included), measured on 2026-11-03 against a local `next start`, 390px viewport. By library fingerprint it contains next/image's client code and the HeroVideo component; how the two split was not measured. Not module-exact. The script's file-only gzip size is smaller (about 6.6 kB) because it leaves out response headers.
